correctness.rationale: The exact block identity and carry congruence bound runs in odd and even bases. Explicit witnesses attain those bounds; forced endpoint residues and the two possible carry patterns classify every extremal start. Fourier expansion of the digit-convolution probability proves conditional equidistribution, and a summable geometric tail yields the exact starting-point densities. Full proof in RESULT.md; verify.py checked 2,492,834 finite starting positions plus explicit witnesses in bases 2..30, without substituting finite tests for universal claims.

originality.rationale: The July 2022 decimal-modulus-8 question and October 2023 Waterloo decimal-modulus-11 solution are direct predecessors; the latter already establishes decimal longest length 38 and earliest starting integer 999981. Neither inspected source states the all-base parity-dichotomous length law, every-maximizer classification, or exact densities. Targeted published-finding corpus searches for equivalences and stronger coverage revealed no matching claim, but a negative search is not proof of novelty. The original part is the simultaneous all-base structural and asymptotic classification, not the earlier decimal number.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased general-base theorem could exist; web and semantic-search absence is not uniqueness proof.
A reader may independently generalize the Waterloo argument; originality is asserted only for the explicit combined sharp all-base classification and exact densities, not decimal m=11 maximum.

value.rationale: The selected modulus b+1 is intrinsic: complete b-digit blocks omit exactly one residue modulo b+1. Determining longest zero-avoiding runs in every base gives an unexpected sharp parity change, a complete classification of extremizing carry patterns and exact densities (often extremely small) for infinitely many natural digital arithmetic problems. These quantify phenomena not addressed by the known decimal maximum; no arbitrary unrelated parameters or artificial cutoffs are introduced.
